transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

It is very unlikely to be about to break. Induction hobs naturally make a humming or buzzing noise at high power, especially when using heavy, multi-layer pans that are large enough to cover the zone. This is normal behaviour. Induction hobs only work with magnetic, flat-bottomed pans. If your stockpot is too small for the zone, warped, or made of non-magnetic material (like some aluminium or copper), the hob may struggle to detect it and buzz loudly. 1. Switch off the hob and let it cool.
2. Place a smaller pan you know works well on the other zones onto the same zone that is buzzing.
3. Turn that zone on to high. If the noise stops with the smaller pan, your stockpot was just unsuitable for induction (or too large/warped) - no repair needed. If the noise continues even with a known-good pan, it could be an issue with that specific heating element or power module, and we can look at next steps.

Happy to try that. With my other pans on the same zone it's quiet, it's only the new stockpot (and a cheap frying pan) that buzzes, and it's quieter at 6 and below. The base is a sandwich base, maybe slightly smaller than the ring. Does that point to the pan rather than the hob?

Yes, that points squarely at the pan rather than the hob. The fact that your other pans are quiet on that same zone suggests the hob is working correctly. Induction hobs buzz when the magnetic field interacts with certain types of cookware—especially large pots with sandwich bases or cheap pans that don't have a flat, uniform base. This noise is normal behaviour for induction technology at high power and does not indicate an impending failure. You can safely continue using your stockpot if you are comfortable with the sound; it will likely be quieter at lower settings (as you noted). If the noise bothers you, try ensuring the pot is perfectly centred on the zone or use a slightly larger pan that covers more of the heating ring. There is no repair needed.
